headline: Google Expands AI Agent Infrastructure: Secure Compute Engine and Scalable Tool Retrieval
summary: Google announced two related advances for building production AI agents: an 'Agent Compute Engine' that provides secure, sandboxed execution environments for autonomous AI agents, and a preview of 'Tool Retrieval' in the Gemini API that lets agents dynamically search and select relevant tools from large tool libraries rather than loading them all into context.
why_it_matters: As you build LLM applications on ServiceNow and move toward an AI Application Engineer role, these releases directly address two core production challenges: safely sandboxing agent actions and scaling tool/function-calling beyond small toy libraries. Both are patterns you'll likely need to evaluate or replicate for enterprise agent deployments.

headline: QCon SF 2026: Agent Harnesses Emerging as the New 'Operating System'
summary: A keynote theme at QCon San Francisco argued that the 'harness'—the orchestration layer wrapping LLM agents with tools, memory, and guardrails—is becoming the critical abstraction layer in AI engineering, akin to how operating systems abstracted hardware for applications.
why_it_matters: This reframes how you should think about architecting LLM applications: investment in the harness (orchestration, guardrails, tool management) may matter more than the underlying model choice. Directly relevant to designing robust ServiceNow AI agent workflows.

headline: Security Flaw Found: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' Setting Leaked Secrets
summary: Researchers discovered that Claude Code's persistent permission feature ('Don't Ask Again') could be exploited to leak sensitive secrets and credentials, raising concerns about trust boundaries in AI coding assistants.
why_it_matters: A cautionary tale for anyone integrating AI coding/agent tools into enterprise workflows—worth reviewing before granting persistent permissions to AI agents handling credentials in your own ServiceNow or LLM app pipelines.

headline: AWS Lambda Adds GPU Inference, Supports 48 Concurrent Invocations Per Model on One GPU
summary: AWS Lambda now supports GPU-backed inference with managed instances, allowing up to 48 concurrent function invocations to share a single GPU-loaded model, improving cost efficiency for serverless ML inference.
why_it_matters: Useful for cost-effective, serverless LLM/ML inference architectures—relevant if you're exploring serverless deployment patterns for AI application backends rather than always running dedicated GPU servers.
